title: Smooth the icing on a cake's side with a smoother, on a turntable
instruction: Smooth the icing on the side of the cake with the smoother, then put the smoother back in its block.
context: Icing a cake and smoothing its side is a job most people who have baked for a birthday know, and know going wrong: the side stays ridged, the smoother digs in and bares the cake, or a mark is left where the smoother was taken off. Bakers do it with two hands: one holds a straight-edged smoother still and upright against the side while the other turns the cake on a revolving stand, so that the edge cuts the high places down and fills the low ones with the icing it carries; taking the smoother off without a mark is the last skill. Here the cake is a decorator's foam practice round, iced on its side and combed into ridges, on a real revolving stand that turns freely and stands loose on the bench. The score is read on the icing at the end: how even the side is, with no bare place and enough icing left, the cake still centred and the smoother back in its block.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left. A revolving cake stand (Ateco 612: aluminium top 305 mm across, 127 mm over the bench, on a cast-iron base, 3.0 kg) stands loose on its non-slip pad with its axis at (30, 0); the top turns freely. On it, centred, on a non-slip mat: a decorator's foam practice round, 152 mm across and 102 mm high, white, on a 203 mm cake board. Its side is iced about 5 mm thick with Wilton Creamy White Decorator Icing (medium consistency, 20 to 22 C, tinted pale blue with gel colour) and combed once round with the comb's coarse teeth: ridges 6 mm apart and 3 mm high to low, a take-off scar 2 mm high down the side; the scar's place and an out-of-round of up to 1 mm vary by seed. The smoother (Ateco 1447 decorating comb and icing smoother, aluminium plate 152 x 102 mm) stands on a short edge in the groove of a small beech stand (base 140 x 80 mm, a back leaning 30 degrees) at (17, -20), its straight edge upright. Both arms start in their ready pose.
scoring: Read on the icing at the end of the trial, on the band from 10 mm over the board to 10 mm under the cake's top. 1.0: within any 50 mm of the surface no more than 1.2 mm between high and low (a 50 mm straightedge on the side, up and round: a 1.2 mm feeler does not go under it); no bare place (white foam shows on the blue icing); mean thickness 3 mm or more (a pin gauge at eight places); the cake within 5 mm of the stand's axis; the smoother back in its block; both grippers 3 cm or more from smoother, cake, stand and block. 0.75: the same but for one flaw (one mark at most 2 mm high and 21 mm wide, or one bare place under 2 cm2). 0.5: the ridges are under 1.5 mm on at least half the way round; or the side is even but the smoother is not in its block or a gripper is within 3 cm. 0.25: the edge has cut at least half the band's height on a quarter of the way round. 0: less; or the cake 15 mm or more off the axis, the stand's base 15 mm or more off its place, or more than a third of the band bare. A trial ends when the score has been 1.0 for one second.
reset_notes: Icing: Wilton Creamy White Decorator Icing from its tub, kept closed at room temperature, stirred, used at 20 to 22 C and tinted pale blue. For every trial the side of the foam round is scraped clean, iced again about 5 mm thick with an offset spatula (the icing weighed on: the tub before and after) and combed once round with the coarse teeth of the Ateco 1447, the comb taken off in one place to leave its scar; scraped icing is not reused. The start is checked with a steel rule held upright against the side and feeler gauges at eight places (ridges about 3 mm high to low) and from above against the start picture. The cake is centred on the stand on its mat (a mark on the top); the stand stands on its pad at its mark; the smoother is washed, dried and stood in the beech stand's groove, straight edge upright. A reset takes about 10 minutes.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX. The icing is not a soft body: it is a field of thicknesses on the cake's side (96 cells round, 34 up) changed by rules: the smoother's straight edge cuts what stands above it, carries it as a roll and fills hollows up to 2 mm under it; where it leaves the side the roll stays as a mark; under 1 mm of icing the foam shows. The cut pushes back with an assumed 4 kPa. No slumping, sticking or air pockets; every icing number is assumed, its bench test is in the README.
